title: Joint Forest Management (JFM)
definition: A participatory forest management strategy where the Forest Department and local village communities (Forest Protection Committees) share the responsibility, management, and usufruct rights of forest resources.
importanceInUpsc: JFM is a critical intersection of Environment, Governance, and Social Justice (GS Paper III & II). It tests the evolution of forest policy from colonial 'exclusionary' models to 'participatory' models.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Joint Forest Management.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (FRA) 2006
